sections.title: Question and boundary
sections.text:
What must make the future PHP and Dart SDKs clean, native packages without turning them into
adapters for neighbouring projects?  This finding is repository-grounded.  AzGuard and Chatom
are **reference implementations only**: AgenTools must not import, wrap, or publish contracts for
either project merely because their code was inspected.

sections.title: Evidence: AzGuard (PHP)
sections.text:
| Observation | Evidence | Planning consequence |
|:--|:--|:--|
| The package separates contracts from façade/implementation code and makes the public contract explicit. | `~/projects/packages/azguard/packages/core/src/Contracts/Permission.php:29`; `.../Facades/AzGuard.php:47` | PHP SDK needs an explicit public-surface rule, not phase-labelled source files. |
| Quality is layered: architecture tests, PHPUnit configuration, local development gates and a release workflow. | `~/projects/packages/azguard/tests/ArchTest.php:15,120`; `phpunit.xml:6`; `DEVELOPMENT.md:23`; `.github/workflows/release.yml:13`; `RELEASING.md:12` | Reuse the discipline: architecture/consumer tests and reproducible release checks; do not copy AzGuard’s runtime dependencies or release metadata blindly. |
| AzGuard’s root and package branch-alias versioning can diverge. | `~/projects/packages/azguard/composer.json`; `packages/core/composer.json` | AgenTools needs a docs/source/CI truth gate before release. |

sections.title: Evidence: Chatom (PHP)
sections.text:
| Observation | Evidence | Planning consequence |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Its written architecture calls for a framework-neutral core and separate integration layers. | `~/projects/packages/chatom/docs/architecture/layering-rules.md:14` | `agentools/sdk` stays framework-free; a future Laravel bridge is a separately approved consumer/adapter, not core SDK scope. |
| Some documented extension points have no proven consuming path; source and docs also disagree on an interface result. | `docs/reference/api-snapshot.md:15,66`; `packages/core/src/Contracts/ChatAgent.php:7`; `.../AgentHandler.php:7,14`; `docs/reference/extension-points.md:18` | A stable AgenTools public contract needs both a real production consuming path and a behavioural test (anti-ghost rule). |
| Its runtime pipeline separates durable state transition from effects. | `packages/core/src/Pipeline/SendMessagePipeline.php:16`; `.../Pipes/BroadcastMessage.php:16` | Preserve this as a generic correctness principle for ports/effects; it is not a Chatom integration contract. |
| CI is layered, but its Laravel/Postgres matrix serves Chatom’s product scope. | `.github/workflows/ci.yml:51,101,138` | Do not add Laravel or database matrices to a pure AgenTools SDK merely by analogy. |

sections.title: Evidence: ecosystem doctrine and current AgenTools state
sections.text:
- The ecosystem positions AgenTools as one normative protocol plus two thin native SDKs; CoreX/Axioma
  consume the contracts rather than becoming SDK dependencies: `AgenTools.md:16,30`; plan `§1`.
- The actual package repository still has no tracked PHP/Dart SDK source; phase-like `p01…p10`
  identifiers are bakeoff probes, not intended public filenames. `git ls-files` and
  `bakeoff/README.md` confirm the boundary.
- The root project card says `category: oss`, while the package `LICENSE` and planned Composer
  skeleton say proprietary. `AgenTools.md:2-8`; `~/projects/packages/agentools/LICENSE:1-7`;
  `@plan/phases/P7/phase.json` P7.1. This is an owner decision, not a silent metadata edit.
- `DR-01` labels itself a draft awaiting approval although P3/P4 were authored against it:
  `@plan/knowledge/10_decisions-DR-01_architecture-2026-08.json:1-9`. Its authority must be reconciled before the
  spec is frozen.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.text:
The package should be clean because public package code has a small, named API, no phase or
reference-project naming, no accidental framework dependency, and release evidence that can be
reproduced from a clean checkout.  The existing plan lacked that terminal quality contract; it is
added as P5.3/P11 rather than retroactively treating research artefacts as product code.

`RAG:— (repo-grounded; no external-version or API claim is made in this finding).`
